    Minimalist, stable, modular, fast, and ZK native implementation of the Ethereum protocol in Rust. L1 and L2 execution client.
  • lambdaworks 739 195
    lambdaworks offers implementations for both SNARKs and STARKs provers, along with the flexibility to leverage their individual components for constructing customized SNARKs.
  • cairo-vm 589 222
    cairo-vm is a Rust implementation of the Cairo VM. Cairo (CPU Algebraic Intermediate Representation) is a programming language for writing provable programs, where one party can prove to another that a certain computation was executed correctly without the need for this party to re-execute the same program.
  • data_science_in_julia_for_hackers 122 25
    Data Science in Julia With Hackers
  • concrete 350 22
    Experimental systems language with linear ownership, explicit capabilities, and Lean-checked proofs for supported code.

Hi, I'm Federico

A happy member of the Erlang, ML and Lisp Evangelism Strikeforce. Network protocol RFC fanatic. Distributed systems, data science and finance.

I founded LambdaClass and Ergodic Group. At LambdaClass we build compilers, Ethereum infrastructure, and cryptographic proving systems, mostly in Rust, Erlang, and Lean. Ergodic Group brings together our work in software, finance, and culture, including an animation studio, a vineyard, and a sushi restaurant.

I spend much of my time on formal systems, proofs, and verified kernels. I also read too much about uncertainty, fat tails, and the limits of knowledge. The two interests contradict each other and I'm fine with that.

Currently: building Concrete, working on the solver behind Stabileo, and formalizing extreme value theory in Lean.

Buenos Aires & Barcelona · Website · Email

Built at LambdaClass

  • ⛓️ ethrex. Ethereum execution client in Rust, both L1 and L2
  • 🔐 lambdaworks. Our SNARK/STARK prover library
  • 🧱 Concrete. Experimental systems language with explicit ownership and capabilities, and Lean-checked proofs for supported code
  • 📊 options_portfolio_backtester. Options backtester we use internally
  • ⚙️ cairo_native. Compiles Cairo Sierra down to MLIR
  • 🏛️ cairo-vm. Cairo VM reimplemented in Rust, now maintained by StarkWare
  • 🔮 lambda_ethereum_consensus. Ethereum consensus client in Elixir, built on the BEAM for fault tolerance
  • 🏗️ Stabileo. Structural analysis in the browser, with a Rust solver compiled to WebAssembly. I lead the solver work. Try it
  • 🎓 erlings. Erlang exercises, rustlings-style

Personal Projects

Formal Verification

  • 📉 lean-extremevaluetheory. Extreme value theory and heavy-tailed probability in Lean 4: Fisher–Tippett–Gnedenko, regular variation, Karamata, Breiman
  • 🛠️ lean-compiler-backend. Native compiler backend written in Lean 4, starting as a QBE 1.3 port. Builds and runs real C programs through cproc
  • 🔩 lean4-baremetal. Lean 4 on bare-metal RISC-V, no OS and no libc. Verified SHA-256, a CAN 2.0 parser, and an automotive torque-enable gate
  • 🪤 verified-still-broken. Five Lean proofs that type-check and still sit on real bugs. The bug lives in the spec, the model, or the trusted base

Quantitative Finance

  • 💥 fatcrash. Research toolkit for tail risk, bubble signals, and market regimes. Rust core with Python bindings
  • 💱 forex-centuries. Exchange rate data going back centuries. Useful for volatility research when you don't trust short samples
  • 📈 finance_research. Notebooks on options backtesting, tail hedging, carry strategies
Other tools and experiments
  • 📖 readtube. Turns YouTube videos into typeset ebooks
  • 🗄️ llm-archive. Ingests all my Claude Code and Codex conversations into SQLite, strips the code, keeps the thinking. Search and analysis over months of LLM usage
  • 🎬 media-server. Self-hosted media server, Docker Compose
  • 🗣️ stoa. Send the same prompt to multiple LLMs, compare side-by-side. Native app, Rust + GPU

Books

  • 🦀 Cryptography in Rust for Hackers. From the math foundations up to SNARKs and STARKs, with Rust implementations
  • 🤝 Distributed Consensus in Rust for Hackers. Consensus from crash fault tolerance to Byzantine protocols and modern blockchain consensus
  • 🔏 Practical Cryptography and Distributed Ledgers. Study guide to cryptography and ZK proving systems, with Pablo Deymonnaz and Diego Kingston
  • 📐 Data Science in Julia for Hackers. Open book on applied data science

Reading Lists

I keep curated reading lists for whatever I'm trying to learn.

  • 🐚 spawnedshelter. The best articles, talks, and books for learning Erlang and Elixir
  • 🎲 the_bayes_way. Bayesian statistics
  • 🐘 learning_leptokurtic. Fat tails and kurtosis
  • 🔁 learning_ergodicity_economics. Ergodicity economics lecture notes
  • 💹 learning_economics. Economics books, papers, and courses
More reading lists
  • learning_formal_verification. Lean and TLA+
  • learning_programming_language_theory. Type systems, semantics, compilers
  • learning_systems_and_security. Systems and security
  • learning_network_protocols. Network protocols and RFCs
  • learning_information_theory. Entropy, coding theory, channel capacity
  • learning_mathematics. Mathematics
  • learning_decision_theory. Rationality under uncertainty, growth-optimal strategies
  • learning_game_theory. Game theory and mechanism design
  • learning_complex_systems. Emergence, power laws, networks
  • learning_statistical_mechanics. Statistical mechanics and thermodynamics
  • learning_data_science. Data science
  • learning_biology. Molecular biology, genetics, neuroscience
  • learning_history_and_geopolitics. Economic history and grand strategy
  • learning_history_and_philosophy_of_science. Epistemology and the history of ideas
  • learning_luxury. Philosophy, business strategy, and craft of luxury

Writing

  • ✍️ At the Core of Finance Lies Geometry. In the End, It's All Jensen's Inequality.

Introduction

This is a simple static page built with Django. It displays:

  • Recent Twitter status messages, with messages that start with @'s removed. In other words, no replies, only true messages.
  • Recent posts from a feed URL

I built it for samuelclay.com, but it can be used to power any static pages and can serve as a useful template for starting a site with static media (JavaScript, CSS, HTML, etc).

Dependencies

  1. Django: easy_install django
  2. Mark Pilgrim's Feedparser: easy_install feedparser
  3. Python-Twitter: easy_install python-twitter
